chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sakoony narrated to us, saying: Al-Hudhrami narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abi Muawiyah narrated to us, from his father, from Al-A'mash, from Abi Zibyan, who said: Umar brought an insane woman who had committed adultery, and he ordered that she be stoned. They took her past Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who asked: 'What is this?' They said: 'An insane woman who has committed adultery.' Umar ordered that she be stoned. He said: 'Do not rush.' Then Umar came to him, and he said to him: 'Do you not know that the pen has been lifted from three: from the child until he reaches puberty, from the insane person until he regains sanity, and from the sleeper until he wakes up?'

The compiler of this book said: This hadith came in this manner. The original version of this, narrated from the People of the House (peace be upon them), states: 'When an insane man commits adultery, he is punished. However, when an insane woman commits adultery, she is not punished, because the insane man performs the act, while the insane woman is the one acted upon.'

key_terms.رُفِعَ الْقَلَم: The pen was lifted (idiom for exemption from legal accountability)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in hadd punishment for an insane man versus an insane woman who commits adultery?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Khisal illustrates the juristic distinction in Shia tradition between the active agency of an insane man, who is subject to hadd punishment, and the passive status of an insane woman, who is exempt. It grounds this specific ruling in the broader prophetic principle that the 'pen is lifted' from those lacking full mental capacity, such as children, the insane, and the sleeping. The text clarifies that while general insanity exempts one from punishment, the specific legal mechanism for women relies on their typical role as the recipient in the act of zina.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-40 Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-Sakoony narrated that Al-Hazrami quoted Ibrahim ibn Abi Muawiyah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-A’amash, on the authority of Abi Zebyan, “An insane woman who had committed adultery was brought to Umar. Umar order that she be stoned to death. They took her to Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB). The Imam (MGB) asked, ‘What is going on?’ They said, ‘She is a crazy woman who has committed adultery. Umar has ordered her to be punished.’ The Imam (MGB) said, ‘Do not rush to do so.’ Then the Imam (MGB) told Umar, ‘Don’t you know that three people are not subject to the rules? They are children until they mature, crazy people until they become sane, and people who are asleep until they wake up.”

The compiler of the book - may God be pleased with him - said, “This tradition appeared here this way. The original version of this tradition that has been narrated on the authority of the Divine Leaders (MGB) says, ‘When an insane man commits adultery, he should be punished. However, when an insane woman commits adultery, she should not be punished. That is because an insane man does the act (of adultery), while an insane woman would be the subject (of adultery).”
